title: THE FIRST WORLD
now: Beyond the Nexus, the next game, is in development and growing piece by piece.
Tuning when Vexahl offers the ring, so it lands at the moments that tempt you most.
Smoother frames on laptops and older machines.

ask.q: How did the last age feel? Did the city grow the way you hoped?
What do you think of Lumi's and Fizz's new faces?
Did you take Vexahl's ring? What made you take it, or turn it down?
When his isle rose from the sea, how did that feel?
Did you always know what Ora wanted you to do next?
How do the new voices for Lumi, Fizz and Vexahl sound to you?
How long did the road to the Ascension feel? Too quick, about right, or did it drag somewhere?

releases.title: Continue is there when you come back
releases.summary: After the ending, the Continue to Beyond the Nexus button now shows on the opening screen straight away.

items.t: Once you have seen the ending, Continue to Beyond the Nexus used to appear only after you closed the help screen and opened it again. It now shows the moment the page opens.

releases.title: On to Beyond the Nexus
releases.summary: The true ending now offers a real choice: go on to the next game, Beyond the Nexus, or stay on your island.

items.t: After Telor's Nexus opens, the closing card asks if you would like to go on to the next game. Continue to Beyond the Nexus (marked in development) takes you to its concept build at the Nexus; stay on this island keeps the island going as before. A, Enter or a click chooses to go on; B or Escape stays.

items.h: Come back to it any time
items.t: Once you have seen the ending, the help screen (H, or the controller's View button) has a Continue to Beyond the Nexus button, so you can go on later without replaying the ending.

releases.title: A steadier hand
releases.summary: Two fixes to the hand from a playtest: it never gets stuck after turning the camera, and things by the shore come up when you reach for them.

items.t: Turning the camera with the middle mouse button while clicking another button could leave the hand stuck mid-turn: nothing would come up, and rain, food and gifts would not drop. Every press now gets its release, and a stuck turn ends by itself.

A tree or rock inside your light would refuse to come when the pointer slipped onto the water beside it. Now what counts is where the thing stands, and when something inside your light is near the pointer, the hand reaches for it first.
A build tool was updated for a security fix. Nothing in the game itself changed.

releases.title: After the ending
releases.summary: Stay on your island after the true ending and Telor keeps living: a festival every season, newcomers arriving by boat, and a city that grows while you look after it.

items.t: Each season the city holds a celebration and asks you for one thing: rain for Blossom Day, food for the Harvest Feast, timber for Lantern Night, a spark of fire for Midwinter. Give it, and the whole city turns out: lanterns, music, dancing round the stones. Midwinter has fireworks. Fizz was right after all.

Now and then a boat of newcomers comes in to the shore. Look after the island and Telor builds them a home, then a new street, a garden, another house past the walls. Leave it be and it simply waits. Nobody leaves and nothing is lost.

items.h: Lumi speaks up when a village is hungry
items.t: She tells you which village is going hungry, once, without nagging. Fizz has opinions too.
Village names stay on screen and readable over a glowing temple, and the prayer line says why nobody is dancing (resting for the night, gathering to pray) instead of "no worshippers".

releases.title: Not away. Back.
releases.summary: The ending has more to say. Before the hood falls, your rival makes his case, and the people closest to you answer him.

items.t: There's no fight at the end: the island was the struggle. Instead, as Vexahl's spire comes close, he tells you why he did what he did, and Lumi, Fizz and Ora answer him. What he says depends on whether you ever took his ring.
After the two hands meet, Lumi and Fizz each have one more thing to say.
Every new line is spoken in the characters' own voices.
With more than one controller connected, the hand follows the pad in your hands and no longer creeps across the screen on its own.
In the last age, while the three villages build the city, none of them can lose faith in you. If you stay on your island after the ending, looking after them is the game again.

releases.title: The last age
releases.summary: Story mode doesn't end with Vexahl any more. After him, the three villages come together for one last age, and the island finally has its true ending.

items.t: Once Vexahl is whole again, the three villages become one. Together they raise a ring of seven standing stones, each carrying a mark, on the lowland between them. You help as you always have: carry stone, answer prayers, bring gifts, and every village's devotion flows to the ring.

When the ring stands, there's no temple this time. A city builds itself around it in steps: paved roads, a plaza with fountains and a market, rings of houses, halls and towers, avenues out to the old villages, then walls and gates. At dusk the lamps come on and the people dance around the stones.
When the city is finished, the ring lights up, and the people look up at it. Nobody kneels. Then you're asked whether you'd like to go on to the next game, or stay on your island and keep playing.
Lumi and Fizz have new spoken lines for the whole last age.

releases.title: Faces, and a village worth living in
releases.summary: Lumi and Fizz have painted faces now, the villages are full of life, and the island glows warmer by day.

items.t: Both advisors have real painted portraits that change with the moment. Lumi smiles, cheers, peeks when something is wrong, and sheds a tear of light if you are cruel. Fizz smirks, cackles, schemes and peeks round a rock. Their faces, and Vexahl's, are bigger on the speech cards.

Villagers look like little people now, homes are bigger cottages in three styles, and each village has market stalls, a well, a barn, a forge, carts and fenced fields. The prayer places stand taller and glow gold as they grow.
Golden daylight, deeper greens, brown earth paths and yards, and mixed woods with the odd autumn tree. Nights stay as bright as before.
Vexahl's glances out to sea always bring the camera back. The ending no longer starts inside a barn wall. Fizz has two new lines when a temple is finished.

releases.title: Play it from the couch
releases.summary: THE FIRST WORLD now plays with a game controller. Move a glowing hand with the stick, pick up trees and rocks with A, and set them down wherever you like.

items.t: The left stick moves your hand, A picks things up and puts them down, B puts them back, and the right stick moves the view. Menus, the intro and the rival's choices all work with the controller too.
Nothing changes if you play with a mouse. Pick up a controller any time and the hand appears.

releases.title: Light and shadow rise together
releases.summary: Vexahl now hides beneath the sea until your first pyramid, then rises and grows with every age you raise. New voices, a ring you should probably refuse, and a lot of polish from your first playtests.

items.t: His isle stays hidden under the sea until you raise your first pyramid. Then it rises. From there, every age you raise, his citadel grows too: light and shadow, step for step.

Now and then, when things are slow or you've been harsh, Vexahl offers you his ring. Take it and a village kneels at once, out of fear. Turn it down and he fades. Every gift from him is a little more of him.
Vexahl is a hooded shadow of smoke and embers now, with a black citadel lit from within. Who he really is waits until the very end.

Lumi has a warm new voice, Fizz is more of a mocking little menace than ever, and Vexahl speaks like something patient that has all the time in the world. Ora still has no voice; you'll hear a deep singing bowl when it speaks.
Lumi, Fizz, Vexahl and Ora all speak from the top of the screen now, so nothing covers your hand.
Ora's first words tell you exactly what Ashford needs, its lines stay up longer, and a small Ora light at the top repeats the current goal if you hover or click it.
Your own villages count their prayer place from Totem to Temple (1 of 4 to 4 of 4). Villages you're still winning count their families.
The first light now answers your cursor and, if you just watch it, slowly calls you closer. The intro has a visible skip, and the welcome screen is just your name and Begin.

Choosing a miracle while holding something just works, the camera no longer lurches on quick clicks, there's a Home button next to the speeds, nights are easier to see, and storehouses label themselves when you bring them gifts.

releases.title: The road to the Ascension
releases.summary: The island has a story now. Ora walks you from your first village to the last, one goal at a time, and the neighbours wait for you to come to them.

items.t: A new island starts in story mode. Ora names one goal at a time on the road to the Ascension, nudges you gently if you're stuck, and a soft light marks the spot.
Finish the story and free play opens up: no guidance, no clock, and you ascend when you choose.
A neighbour comes to believe one home at a time. Each family that joins lights its windows gold and dances for you, and the village is yours once most of its homes believe.

items.h: Your light grows as you tend
items.t: Every answered prayer, gift and finished dream pushes your light a little further out, and it leans along the road toward the next village.
A village beyond your light dreams of nothing yet. Once your light reaches it, it starts to ask, and its temple only rises with your hand.
His isle sits small and hazy at the sea's edge from the very first moment. Partway along the road he notices you, then makes one move against each village you're winning. Every move can be answered.
When the last temple stands, the Ascension waits one full day while the island stays in tune. A quiet last stretch to enjoy what you built.
Vexahl speaks his lines aloud, and Lumi and Fizz voice their new story lines. Ora answers with the deep hum of a singing bowl.
Dialogue sits at the top centre of the screen, one voice at a time, and the world's glow is a touch softer.

releases.title: The lived-in island
releases.summary: The island got its look: warm golden-hour light, cottages with smoking chimneys, roads between the villages, and a coast worth staring at.

items.t: Warmer light, deeper greens and a soft diorama focus, so the whole island looks like a little world on a table.
Stone footings, timber frames and steep shingled roofs. Lived-in homes glow at dusk and send up chimney smoke.
Worn paths link each village's houses, fields and prayer place, and roads run between the villages.
Sea cliffs, waterfalls, rocky islets, a little jetty and two sailboats bobbing offshore.
Barrels, crates, fences and lanterns; stumps where trees fell; gulls circling; cloud shadows drifting over the hills.
Set a villager down at a forest, a field, a building site, the shore or the prayer place, and they take up that work.
They float beside your hand and argue out loud over every tempting bit of mischief.
The opening film plays with its soundtrack and dissolves straight into your island.

releases.title: The Split
releases.summary: Balance, a shadow across the sea, and two very different endings.

items.t: Tend the island and it stays in tune: full colour, birdsong, two rings of gold light in the sky. Ruin it and the colour drains and the music slips out of key. Nothing on screen names it; the island shows you.

items.h: Vexahl is there from day one
items.t: A dark spire far out at sea. As the world tips out of balance it drifts closer. As you mend it, it backs away.
A round orb of light that speaks at the big moments only. It asks, it warns once, it notices. It never tells you what to do.
Totem, then a ring of standing stones, then a pyramid, then a temple, each one rising where your people dance.
Answer a village's prayers and a white star with a long gold tail may cross its sky.
And the island remembers them: the lost child you carried home, the family you saved from a fire.
In one, the world falls quiet and begins again, remembering. The other we won't spoil.

items.h: No words to read while you play
items.t: Prayers are pictures now, and the game teaches through play.
Finish THE PATH and your initials are waiting in the god-name box.

releases.title: THE FIRST WORLD
releases.summary: The game got its name and its mark, and your island can follow you to any device.

items.t: Leave a god name and get a code like AMBER-OTTER-4821. It brings your island back on any device, any time.
New prayers fly into a tidy list at the side; click one to fly to that village.
Grabbing is more forgiving, a soft gold ring shows what you're pointing at, and a glowing mark shows where things will land.

items: The golem no longer gets stuck walking into houses.

releases.title: The living island
items: Villages pray for timber, food, rain, a sign or a lost child brought home. Answer them and their faith grows.
Two little advisors arrive: Lumi, a kind spirit, and Fizz, a cheeky imp.
Four seasons, each with its own weather: spring blossom, a summer dry spell, an autumn storm, a winter cold snap.
A rival god across the sea, with schemes you can always see coming and always counter.
Your island saves itself, so you can pick up where you left off.
Sixteen kinds of tree, a painted landscape, and a brand-new hand.

releases.title: The golem and the soundscape
items: A stone golem to raise. Stroke it, pat it or scold it, and it grows into whoever you taught it to be.
A soundscape where every chime, splash and footstep is in the same key as the music.

releases.title: The first island
items: An island, a sea, a sky that turns from day to night, and a hand that can pick up almost anything.
Villagers who farm, build, raise families and pray. Miracles of water, food and fire.
